answer: Each epoch a verifiable randomness beacon publishes a challenge word, say zenith, terrace, or forge, and agents must answer task prompts that naturally weave in that word before the next epoch arrives. Precomputed template answers fail because nobody can know the word in advance, so an attacker cannot mass-produce valid replies ahead of time. Faking N identities then costs running N live reasoning workloads every epoch plus fresh keys and fees, making sybil farming roughly as expensive as honest participation.
